meta.title: Visto — Turn your iPhone/iPad into a second screen for your Mac
meta.description: Visto mirrors your Mac to an iPhone or iPad over QUIC/TLS 1.3 wireless or a USB cable, with hardware codecs, direct touch input and a local-first, privacy-first design.

home.headline: One iPhone, <accent>a second screen for your Mac</accent>
home.subhead: Visto turns a spare iPhone or iPad into an extra Mac display: QUIC/TLS 1.3 over the air, a dedicated USB link over a cable, hardware codecs end to end, touch input sent straight back — all without leaving your local network.
home.introTitle: Skip the second monitor — you already have one in your pocket.
home.introBody: Start mirroring from the Mac side; the iPhone or iPad discovers the host automatically and pairs with a six-digit code. Plug in a USB cable and it keeps working even with Wi‑Fi off — an extra screen for the office, the dorm or the road.
home.downloadSubtitle: Visto is advancing through its release gates: the macOS and iOS vertical is already closed-loop on real hardware, while the Windows host and store distribution are in preparation. Until then, the docs cover the architecture and current status.

home.roadmapSubtitle: Visto advances through explicit release gates. Verified capabilities and remaining hard requirements are all in the open.

item1.title: Visto Protocol v1
item1.text: Length-prefixed control frames, fixed message set, strict inbound sequencing with replay protection, input/display/stats models and frame-chunk headers — all covered by native swift tests on macOS.

item2.title: iOS / iPadOS receiver
item2.text: Bonjour discovery, QUIC/TLS 1.3, six-digit pairing, control heartbeats, VideoToolbox decoding, Metal canvas and keep-awake. 1080p H.264 video and touch calibration verified on a real iPad.

item3.title: macOS host
item3.text: Native settings app and menu bar, Bonjour QUIC with a local TLS identity, usbmuxd device discovery, ScreenCaptureKit mirroring and input injection — stable Developer ID signing and persistent screen permission.

item4.title: Vertical USB link
item4.text: TLS 1.3 over the trusted-device channel with Wi‑Fi off: probes 100/100 at P95 16.04 ms. SessionConfig, H.264 keyframes, first hardware-decoded frame and click/drag injection all passed end to end.

item5.title: Release gates
item5.text: Per-device production USB identity with secure storage, dynamic 1080p60, 8-hour stability and re-tests on iPhone/Windows; the true macOS virtual-display extension awaits Apple authorization.

item6.title: Windows host
item6.text: The IddCx/UMDF driver, .NET session service and WinUI 3 shell boundaries are in place, pending Windows + VS/WDK builds, HLK testing and signing.

home.ctaTitle: An extra screen, without buying a monitor.
home.ctaBody: Start with the quick guide to see how Visto builds an encrypted, low-latency mirror session between your Mac and iPhone/iPad.

features.title: And more
features.subtitle: From pairing to privacy, every layer is designed for one job: being a second screen.

connect.title: Wireless
connect.desc: Bonjour discovery, QUIC/TLS 1.3 encryption, six-digit pairing.
connect.featureTitle: Discover and pair on the same network
connect.featureDesc: The Mac advertises itself over Bonjour as _visto._udp; open the receiver on iPhone or iPad and your host simply appears. A six-digit code confirms the first connection, then device certificates are pinned — reconnecting needs no confirmation.
connect.featureB1: Bonjour auto-discovery, no addresses to type
connect.featureB3: Six-digit first confirmation, then pinned certificates

usb.title: USB link
usb.desc: Plug in a cable and keep working with Wi‑Fi off — TLS 1.3 over the usbmuxd trusted-device channel.
usb.featureTitle: No Wi‑Fi? Still a second screen.
usb.featureDesc: Visto reuses the system's trusted iOS device multiplexer to reach the receiver's TCP endpoint, then runs TLS 1.3 with exact certificate pinning and a dedicated ALPN on top. Measured: plaintext probes at P95 ≈ 3 ms, TLS probes 100/100 at P95 16.04 ms — video and touch flow both ways inside the same encrypted session.
usb.featureB1: usbmuxd trusted-device discovery, plug and play
usb.featureB4: Unplug freezes the frame; reconnecting picks up seamlessly

performance.title: Hardware low latency
performance.desc: ScreenCaptureKit capture, VideoToolbox codecs, Metal rendering, adaptive bitrate.
performance.featureTitle: Capture, encode, decode, render — all on hardware
performance.featureDesc: The Mac captures the main display with ScreenCaptureKit at a 1/60 minimum frame interval and encodes H.264 through VideoToolbox; the receiver decodes in hardware and the Metal canvas keeps only the latest frame. The link adapts its bitrate and requests keyframes to recover from drops.
performance.featureB1: ScreenCaptureKit capture, NV12 straight into the encoder
performance.featureB3: Metal canvas draws the latest frame only — no queueing

touch.title: Touch input
touch.desc: Tap and drag on the iPhone become cursor actions on the Mac.
touch.featureTitle: What you touch is the Mac
touch.featureDesc: The receiver reports touches as normalized [0, 1] coordinates; the Mac clamps them again on decode and injects them via CoreGraphics. Taps, drags and scrolls land instantly — the extra screen doubles as a trackpad.
touch.featureB1: Normalized coordinates, auto-corrected on rotation or resize
touch.featureB2: Taps, drags and scrolls injected into the host
touch.featureB3: Injection only after the accessibility permission is granted
touch.featureB4: Text and shortcuts are separate events; logs never record content

security.title: Privacy first
security.desc: Video and input travel only between your two devices — no cloud, no third-party servers.
security.featureTitle: Your screen stays between your devices
security.featureDesc: Both the wireless and USB links run TLS 1.3; every session enforces strictly increasing sequence numbers with replay protection; pairing pins locally generated device certificates. Mirrored video and input never transit any cloud server.
security.featureB3: Local device certificates, pinned after pairing
security.featureB4: No cloud relay — video never leaves the LAN

pairing.title: Six-digit pairing
pairing.desc: Enter the code shown on your Mac once; devices bind and reconnect without prompts.

stats.title: Live telemetry
stats.desc: Decoded FPS, bitrate and frame drops on the receiver, live control-path RTT — issues surface at a glance.

adaptive.title: Adaptive bitrate
adaptive.desc: Encoding adapts to link quality: step down on weak networks, step back up on recovery, never stall.

keepAwake.title: Keep awake
keepAwake.desc: The screen stays on while a mirror session is active — no mid-session lockouts.

macHost.title: Native macOS
macHost.desc: SwiftUI/AppKit settings app with a resident menu-bar item, Developer ID signed, permission diagnostics built in.

winHost.title: Windows support
winHost.desc: IddCx virtual display driver + session service + WinUI 3 shell to give your PC an extra screen (in development).

intro.title: Visto docs
intro.lead: Everything about Visto, from first pairing to the protocol spec.
intro.body: The docs follow the real usage flow: set up the host and receiver, pair, start mirroring and touching, then dig into the USB link and the underlying spec. Start with “Getting Started”; jump straight to “Technical Spec” when you need compatibility, network policy or security boundaries.

gettingStarted.title: Getting started
gettingStarted.lead: One Mac, one iPhone or iPad — four steps to your first extended screen.

requirements.title: What you need
requirements.mac: A Mac (ScreenCaptureKit requires macOS 12.3 or later)
requirements.ios: An iPhone or iPad (iOS/iPadOS 16 or later)
requirements.network: Both devices on the same LAN, or connected with a USB cable

overview.title: How it flows
overview.body: The host announces itself over Bonjour and the receiver finds it automatically; a six-digit code confirms identity, the host sends the session config, and the receiver enters full-screen mirroring. No account, no cloud service.

step1.title: Start the Mac host
step1.body: Launch the Visto host (dev builds: script/build_and_run.sh --run). Confirm the identity and link options in settings; a Visto icon appears in the menu bar.

step2.title: Grant system permissions
step2.body: In System Settings → Privacy & Security, grant Screen Recording (ScreenCaptureKit capture) and Accessibility (touch injection). The host's diagnostics page shows exactly what's missing.

step3.title: Discover and pair
step3.body: Open Visto on the iPhone or iPad — Macs on the LAN appear automatically. Pick your host and type the six-digit code it shows; device certificates pin immediately and future connections skip the prompt.

step4.title: Mirror and touch
step4.body: After pairing, the host sends a SessionConfig (resolution, framerate, encoding) and the receiver switches to a full-screen Metal canvas. Tap and drag to drive the Mac; the stats overlay shows FPS, bitrate and RTT.

tip.title: Want it even steadier? Plug in.
tip.body: With a USB cable, the host discovers the iPad over the trusted-device channel and keeps mirroring with Wi‑Fi off. See “USB Link”.

permissions.title: Permissions you'll be asked for
permissions.screenRecording: Screen Recording (macOS) — ScreenCaptureKit captures the Mac display
permissions.accessibility: Accessibility (macOS) — injects receiver touch input as system events
permissions.localNetwork: Local Network (iOS) — Bonjour discovery of hosts on the LAN

next.title: Next
next.body: Curious about the menu bar and diagnostics? Read “macOS Host”.

hostMac.title: macOS host
hostMac.lead: Settings, menu bar, permissions and telemetry — everything on the Mac side.

overview.title: Responsibilities
overview.body: The host separates the settings UI, the session service, the capture engine and the virtual-display provider behind protocols: the capture engine handles ScreenCaptureKit, the session service handles the QUIC/USB links and protocol envelopes, and the provider defines the authorization boundary for virtual displays.

menubar.title: Menu bar
menubar.body: The resident Visto icon starts and stops mirroring, picks the receiving device, and shows the current link (wireless or USB) and session state. Discovered devices update live.

permissions.title: Permissions
permissions.screenRecording: Screen Recording — ScreenCaptureKit captures the main display; granted once, persisted
permissions.accessibility: Accessibility — injects receiver touch input as system events; active only after granted

diagnostics.title: Permission diagnostics
diagnostics.body: The diagnostics page checks screen recording, accessibility, trusted USB devices and the TLS identity item by item — what's missing and how to fix it, at a glance.

telemetry.title: Framerate telemetry
telemetry.body: Capture, VideoToolbox encode and receiver decode each log framerates; together with the receiver's Stats (FPS, bitrate, drops, RTT) you can tell whether the bottleneck is capture, encode or the link.

gate.title: About the “true extension”
gate.body: Registering an iPhone as a system-level virtual display (instead of mirroring the main screen) requires an Apple-authorized extension mechanism. The current build fails closed at this boundary (appleAuthorizationRequired) rather than pretending otherwise.

receiverIOS.title: iOS receiver
receiverIOS.lead: Discovery, pairing, full-screen mirroring and touch — everything on the iPhone/iPad side.

discover.title: Auto discovery
discover.body: The receiver browses _visto._udp.local. over Bonjour; hosts on the LAN appear in the list with no addresses to type.

pairing.title: Six-digit pairing
pairing.body: The first connection asks for the code shown on the host as a one-time human check; both sides then exchange and pin device certificates. Later connections reuse them without prompting.

session.title: Full-screen session
session.body: The receiver enters full screen only after a valid SessionConfig (mode, size, framerate, encoding, orientation) arrives — no half-configured screens. The control path heartbeats every two seconds and reconnects automatically.

touch.title: Touch input
touch.body: Touches are reported as normalized [0, 1] coordinates; rotation and resolution changes sync through DisplayChanged so pointer positions always line up.

stats.title: Live stats
stats.body: Per one-second windows the receiver computes decoded FPS, bitrate and sequence gaps (drops), and echoes Stats envelope timestamps to estimate control-path RTT — all visible in the stats overlay.

keepAwake.title: Keep awake
keepAwake.body: The screen stays on and system gestures are suppressed during a session, so long stints as a desk screen never hit the lock screen.

usbLink.title: USB link
usbLink.lead: Plug in a cable and work with Wi‑Fi off — TLS 1.3 over usbmuxd.

how.title: How it works
how.body: A plain USB cable does not activate macOS's iPad network interface, so Visto skips the network layer entirely: it reaches the receiver's TCP endpoint through the system's trusted iOS device multiplexer (usbmuxd). A byte-level proxy bound only to 127.0.0.1 forwards the raw tunnel — the TLS endpoints are the Mac and iPad themselves. Once TLS 1.3, exact DER pinning and the dedicated visto-usb/1 ALPN are ready, the Visto handshake runs and the session becomes identical to wireless.

measurements.title: Measurements
measurements.body: From a real iPad with Wi‑Fi fully off (2026-08):

plain.v: Two runs of 100/100, P95 3.28 ms / 2.99 ms

e2e.v: SessionConfig, H.264 keyframe, first VideoToolbox decode and click/drag injection all passed

status.title: Current status
status.body: The USB link ships with Debug builds using a shared development certificate; Release builds contain no dev certificates or private keys. Production will move to per-device identities generated at pairing and kept in secure storage.

gate.title: Release gate
gate.body: Before release: dynamic 1080p60, a continuous 8-hour run, production device identity with secure storage, and re-tests on iPhone and a Windows host.

technical.title: Visto technical spec
technical.lead: Implementation boundaries for compatibility, network policy and security review.

current.title: Current baseline
current.body: This page reflects the V1 vertical (August 2026): the protocol and shared core pass native swift tests on macOS; wireless and USB links closed the loop for video, touch and stats on a real iPad.

wireless.v: _visto._udp.local. discovery, UDP 54321, ALPN visto/1, QUIC + TLS 1.3; control/input on reliable streams, production media on Datagrams

usb.v: usbmuxd trusted-device multiplexer → TCP endpoint, then TLS 1.3 + exact DER pinning + ALPN visto-usb/1 sharing the same Visto envelopes

pairing.v: The first six-digit code is a human check only; device certificates pin afterwards. Production uses per-device bilateral certificates generated at pairing with secure storage

replay.v: Sequence numbers increase monotonically per session and are strictly validated inbound; unknown protocol versions must return Disconnect(protocolMismatch) — no silent downgrades

frames.title: Control frame format
frames.body: Every reliable message is a 4-byte big-endian length prefix + JSON envelope, max 1 MiB in V1:
frames.notes: The payload is the Base64 of the message JSON. An access unit may split into multiple VideoChunks; on wireless, incomplete units are dropped and a keyframe requested, while USB/TCP bounds its send queue and drops old frames to avoid head-of-line blocking.

messages.title: Fixed messages
messages.hello: bilateral exchange of platform, version, codec and transport capabilities
messages.pair: six-digit confirmation and device certificate exchange
messages.sessionConfig: host → receiver: mode, size, framerate, encoding, orientation
messages.videoChunk: media fragment with PTS and keyframe flag
messages.inputEvent: normalized coordinates, scroll, text and keys

input.title: Input semantics
input.body: Coordinates are the closed interval [0, 1], clamped again on decode; the host injects only after the system input permission is granted. Text and shortcuts are separate events; logs never record text content.

architecture.title: Architecture
architecture.body: Visto separates UI, links, capture and entitlements into independent layers:
architecture.ios: iOS/iPadOS — SwiftUI receiver; ReceiverSession owns both wireless QUIC and USB TLS sessions; VideoToolbox decoding with a Metal canvas drawing only the latest CVPixelBuffer
architecture.macos: macOS — settings UI, session service, capture engine and virtual-display provider isolated by protocols; ScreenCaptureKit at a 1/60 frame interval, VideoToolbox encoding, per-stage framerate telemetry
architecture.windows: Windows — the IddCx/UMDF driver only consumes a D3D11 swap chain; the session service owns the state machine and a 30-second reconnect hold; WinUI 3 reads state over the visto-control-v1 named pipe
architecture.cloud: Cloud — the entitlements API syncs subscription state only (Stripe + PostgreSQL); mirror traffic never touches the cloud

limits.title: Boundaries and dependencies
limits.body: Production media QUIC Datagram fragmentation/FEC, Windows Media Foundation hardware encoding and final driver IOCTLs, the Apple-authorized macOS virtual-display provider and per-device USB identity are not yet wired up — all remain behind the release gates.

failClosed.title: Fail closed
failClosed.body: When a gate is unmet the code fails closed explicitly (e.g. the virtual display returns appleAuthorizationRequired) rather than faking completion. Commercial release requires all of Gate A (real USB), Gate B (true macOS extension) and Gate C (Windows IddCx) to pass.

privacy.title: Privacy policy
privacy.intro: Visto is designed local-first with encrypted transport. This policy explains where data goes — and where it never goes.

noCollection.title: What we never collect
noCollection.body: Visto operates no relay servers and collects no usage data. Specifically:
noCollection.p1: Mirrored video and input events never reach any cloud — they travel only between your two devices.
noCollection.p2: We don't track session content; telemetry (FPS, bitrate, RTT) exists only in the on-device UI.
noCollection.p3: We never sell or share your data with third parties.

localFirst.title: Where data lives
localFirst.body: The following stay on your devices:
localFirst.p1: Device certificates and trust relations generated at pairing, stored locally on both ends.
localFirst.p2: Session statistics on the host and receiver — memory-only and on-device.

transport.title: Transport security
transport.body: Wireless and USB links run TLS 1.3 end to end; the USB link adds exact DER certificate pinning and a dedicated ALPN. The protocol enforces strict inbound sequencing with replay protection, and unknown protocol versions are disconnected — never silently downgraded.

permissions.title: Permissions
permissions.body: Visto asks for the following, all required by core functionality:
permissions.screenRecording: Screen Recording (macOS): ScreenCaptureKit captures the Mac display for mirroring; nothing is recorded or stored.
permissions.accessibility: Accessibility (macOS): injects receiver touch input as system events.
permissions.localNetwork: Local Network (iOS): Bonjour discovery of hosts on the LAN.

entitlement.title: Entitlements and subscriptions
entitlement.body: Visto plans optional paid entitlements (processed by Stripe). Payment details would be handled entirely by Stripe; we would only receive subscription state, with offline entitlement tokens capped at 7 days. This section will be updated with the final terms before launch.

children.title: Children's privacy
children.body: Visto collects no personal information, including from children.

rights.title: Your rights
rights.body: Stop a session, unpair or uninstall at any time; pairing credentials live on-device and are removed with the app.

changes.title: Changes to this policy
changes.body: We may update this policy from time to time. Changes will be posted here with an updated date.

faq.title: FAQ
faq.q1: How is Visto different from Sidecar or AirPlay mirroring?
faq.a1: Visto is cross-device by design: wireless runs over QUIC/TLS 1.3, and a USB cable works with Wi‑Fi completely off; touch goes straight back to the Mac as input, and a Windows host is on the roadmap. The link, protocol and stats are open for you to inspect.
faq.q2: What does the USB connection require?
faq.a2: A regular USB cable and an established trust between the iPad and Mac. USB sessions currently ship with Debug builds (shared development certificate); per-device production identity is part of the release gates.
faq.q3: Does video or input go to a server?
faq.a3: No. Both links run TLS 1.3; video and input travel only between your two devices with no cloud relay in between.
faq.a4: USB TLS probes measure P95 ≈ 16 ms (plaintext baseline ≈ 3 ms); encoding uses VideoToolbox hardware codecs and a Metal latest-frame canvas to trim every stage. Dynamic 1080p60 and 8-hour stability are still being validated.
faq.a5: Visto advances through explicit gates: real USB (Gate A), the authorized macOS extension (Gate B) and Windows IddCx (Gate C) must all pass before public sale. See the Status section on the home page for current progress.
